filters.correction: Never corrected. Values must match; matching capacity case addresses also requires the receiver's capacity-selection relation. Equal geometry does not authorize bank migration, and differing storage contracts refuse under every policy, including the Recovery family override.
filters.description: Compares the observed storage contract: H8 bank markers or addresses and spacing, ATA flash or serial ranges, or SCSI serial records. It does not establish physical flash capacity, erase boundaries or safe migration. Correction requires complete copy, erase, commit and recovery proof.
filters.name: Storage geometry

policies.text: Matching geometry does not imply a matching parameter layout; the persistent parameter layout is a separate required filter.
A storage reader that is not recognized, or that needs resident code which is not supplied, stays Unresolved; no default geometry is assumed.

filters.description: Compares role-bound native closed/open input predicates (address, encoding, bit and active level), or a supported architecture-specific initialization program. Predicates do not prove a sensor count or cover every output, configuration or feedback role. Shared sub-roles can overlap Loading observations without establishing equivalent wiring or mechanical states. Correction would need those residual roles and all affected movement/error paths bound.
filters.name: Startup inputs

policies.text: The value is chosen by the native reader that resolves, not by the SAT digit: equal tray input predicates compare equal across SAT8 and SAT9. The constant E46B initialization store is evidence only; SAT8 and SAT9 never fall back to it, so unresolved predicates stay Unresolved.
SAT1 has no recognized tray input reader and keeps its native E46B register value (bits 4 and 0) or its older initialization program.

V850 slim drives: the value is the loading program's fixed direct I/O, plus the fixed outputs of directly called helpers followed exactly one level when the direct set lacks an output. Deeper, indirect or byte-wide helper paths are not bound (they are named as evidence), and equality means the same bound I/O set.
An architecture tag, an external initializer address or an unexamined program is not a known value. Such images stay Unresolved and receive no family ID.

filters.correction: Never corrected. Values must match; no host-setup correction is implemented.
filters.description: Compares observed host setup: masked H8 FE94 bit 7, a bound older initializer, or architecture-specific host/reset coordinates. The bit is an observation, not an established voltage or protocol mode. Correction requires the physical meaning and Normal/Kernel reset and resume behavior to be established.
filters.name: Host setup

policies.text: A detector miss is never an absent host or an invented FE94 zero; it stays Unresolved.

FE94 bit 7 is not corrected because it follows the board's host connection (written 0xC0 by every USB-bridged external drive, 0x40 by every native-SATA drive) and the same native host bring-up also changes the ATAPI transport register FEC0 (0xC6 vs 0xC7), whose bit 0 the Kernel link-event handler drives at runtime, so a one-bit FE94 edit would not make the incoming host setup match the installed board.

filters.description: Compares a native interrupt-controller operation, physical loading-input predicate or installed callback route; the variant is part of the value. A selected controller observation does not describe every installed vector or callback; supporting observations do not widen that value. Direct writes and masked updates have different state effects. Correction would also need the installed vector/callback, polling, acknowledgement and mechanical contracts bound.
filters.name: Loading / IRQ

policies.text: Additional recognizer misses are not proof of absence and are never hashed as negative facts.

FFC5 write 0x20 versus clear bit 5 is not correctable because the clear belongs to a peripheral driver that the 0x20 firmware entirely lacks: it unmasks interrupt-controller source 0x200040 and ASIC line FFFDFF29 bit 7 for a serial-attached device's fault-report interrupt, initialized over F904/F950-F953. Matching FFC5 would mean adding or removing that driver, and held bytes do not show whether the other board carries or can do without that device. Neither FFC5 operation is a loading input; both families poll their tray switch elsewhere.

filters.correction: Never corrected. Any known layout difference refuses. Where the installed record region overlaps non-erased bytes of the target Normal, the refusal reports that collision.
filters.description: Compares the parameter read contract: address basis and base, record count and size, header size, word encoding and record selection. It does not prove the writer, erase, rollover, initialization or recovery lifecycle. Layout and geometry can be coupled; changing an address alone is not a relocation recipe. Correction would require the complete persistent-data lifecycle and coupled storage contract to remain valid without writing separate persistent data.
filters.name: Parameter layout

policies.text: A layout read through a Kernel-resident reader needs the exact paired Kernel; without it the layout stays Unresolved and the image has no family ID.

filters.correction: Corrects supported incoming Normal channel operands while preserving execution, waveform tables, DSP program, calibration and motion behavior. Architecture and output interface must match. Other filters remain independently enforced.
filters.description: Compares the native output assignment together with architecture and output interface. Supported corrections change only the incoming firmware channel mapping while retaining its DSP program, waveform tables, calibration and motion behavior. This is not a change of drive voltage, motor type or byte-versus-word output interface.
filters.name: Phase

policies.text: Unresolved or conflicting phase refuses. A phase correction authorizes only the phase change: every other registered value must still match, and the corrected image is re-verified.

SAT1 phase correction binds complete native output programs and changes only supported channel operands, preserving output helper execution and unrelated bytes. Forms requiring a call/inline rewrite remain observable but refuse assignment changes because call timing and temporary stack preservation are unproved. Equal assignments need no correction; unrecognized or conflicting programs refuse.

Split-word (F910-F913) correction exchanges the corresponding output and control destinations in complete native programs. Equal phase assignments require no correction, even when other mechanism properties differ. No donor tables, DSP program, calibration policy or persistent values are copied.
M32C corrections need a tail-key Normal, or a boot-key Normal with its Kernel. V850 corrections need sparse-checksum Normal and Kernel files and the exact paired Kernel.
No SCSI phase program is recognized, so phase stays Unresolved and no correction is planned.

filters.correction: H8 startup comparison operands remain unchanged, with a read-only live-word prerequisite for equal known comparisons or a supported unresolved-source target-word fallback. Differing primary comparisons refuse because no complete OEM writer-lifecycle proof is bound. Separately bound non-comparison preservation and other platforms retain their independent native prerequisites.
filters.description: Compares a bound startup gate or a separately proved preservation contract: unchanged H8 word 0x009F comparisons, ATA word 0x00D9, V850 Kernel identity, or SCSI checksum/header. Fixed and conditional predicates differ. No recognised comparison does not mean no requirement; reader, caller, cache, startup-path and automatic OEM writer-lifecycle evidence remain separate. Only the bounded H8 and M32C startup-gate-absent proofs establish that a target has no fixed 0x009F or native 0x00D9 gate.
filters.name: Startup

policies.text: A bound native H8 comparison retains its exact operand and requires a read-only live word. Equal known source and target comparisons retain this prerequisite; differing primary comparisons refuse without a complete automatic OEM writer-lifecycle witness. An unresolved installed comparison can admit an unchanged bound target only with equal Normal-owned reader layouts and a read-only target-word prerequisite. Missing evidence never selects FFFF. Bound native loader-flag inventories establish scoped target-local predicate preservation through the shared verifier; bank selection and the automatic OEM parameter-writer lifecycle are not inferred. Host command, image checksum, generation marker, persistent-bank predicates and independent hardware checks retain their owners. Unknown startup code is preserved only when both Normal and Kernel are unchanged. Recognized native integrity failures and other unresolved transitions refuse. A missing Kernel-resident getter remains unresolved and cannot use the read-only fallback.

Startup gate absent (Not applicable, proof 1): the exact Kernel must be held; every Kernel 0x009F load must be the audited buffer byte store; the Normal getter must be bound with no recognized 0x009F comparison; and either the audited startup function is bound by its unique handler-install anchor with a gate slot that holds no 0x009F read, or only one getter read whose R0 result the next callee overwrites, or, for SAT1 only, stored Normal neither calls nor wraps loader-flag service 0x400A1A and passes 0x009F to no getter call. A gate-absent target never checks the word, so it needs no live-word prerequisite and no edit, whatever the installed side; independent preservation certificates still bind. A gate-absent installed side with a gated target takes exactly the unresolved-installed path. Two gate-absent images match. A missing Kernel or any other shape stays unresolved.
Where a native conditional gate is bound, 0xFE23 is accepted unconditionally and 0xFE09 only when the complete bound predicate holds.
An equal 0x00D9 predicate needs no change; a different one has no approved write recipe and refuses. V850: the paired Kernel must carry the expected Kernel identity.

M32C startup gate absent (Not applicable, proof 1): the exact 16 KiB Kernel must be held with reset vector 0xFFC000 and one acceptance gate (reset-cleared RAM flag 0x3000, word sum of 0x1000..0x2000 and 0xF80010..0xFFC000, 16-byte header) whose transfer is the Normal entry; the entry prefix may hold only memory initialization before its JSR.A to main; main must reach its OS task-install anchor through data writes and direct calls only, with a direct JSR.A in the gate slot; and neither Normal nor Kernel may hold an immediate 0x00D9 index load or a native word-ID getter. Callees are not executed. A gate-absent target needs no word and no edit, whatever the installed side; a gate-absent installed side with a 0x00D9 target takes the unresolved path. Two gate-absent images match. A missing Kernel or any other shape stays unresolved.
The resident checksum and the matching 16-byte image-pair header must hold; otherwise the update refuses.

identity.partition: Families never cross a platform. The identity starts with the platform partition: SAT 1xxx, SAT 8xxx/9xxx (one H8 SAT platform), ATA or SCSI. SAT 8xxx and SAT 9xxx are one platform because their Kernels receive, hand off, finalize, checksum and marker-gate updates with the same native code and their persistent banks use the same versioned contract. Recorder-branded REC 8xxx selects the same H8 native discovery; its raw tag is retained and every hardware contract must still be established and match. A tag outside these domains produces no identity. Under the strict update policy the correction planner also refuses any transition between different platforms before owner corrections are considered.
rules: Every registered filter runs on every image. Hardware filters form the identity; operational requirements are evaluated and planned per update but never enter it.

As-is identity: every hardware value before any correction. Matching (candidate) family: each owner's projection with exactly what it may correct removed, so it is built only from facts no owner corrects.
A required hardware value that is Unresolved or Conflicting produces no family ID. Unresolved values never compare equal; a positive not-applicable proof compares by its proof tag.
Family equality never authorizes a write. Every remaining difference must pass its owner's correction proof, or the pair refuses at that step.
